text:
maria.su: Hey team — my docs PR is blocked, need quick confirmation on header/tracing behavior for Private deployments before I can finalize the SDK snippet. Specifically: do custom tracing headers (e.g. X-Request-ID, X-Traceparent) get propagated through the Private control plane to model logs/observability, or are they stripped/overridden? I'm writing an example curl + JS snippet and want to avoid promising header passthrough if it's not guaranteed.
kevin.l: @maria.su good question. Short answer: for Private (VPC) the control plane preserves custom headers and forwards them to the local agent, but we do sanitize any auth-sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) by default. Tracing headers like X-Request-ID and traceparent are preserved. :white_check_mark:
ajohnson: Quick nuance — hosted API has an extra router that will inject our internal request id header (x-rw-request-id) and may add trace context. In Private, you generally keep your headers intact unless you enable 'control_plane_header_hardening' in config. We're working on docs for that flag.
maria.su: Thanks. What's the exact header name we should show in examples? Should we recommend users set X-Request-ID or use W3C traceparent? I want the snippet to be best-practice.
kevin.l: Recommend W3C traceparent + a stable X-Request-ID as fallback. Example: add both headers. Runtime will correlate traceparent with our traces and keep X-Request-ID on logs.
devex-bot: Reminder: existing docs snippets use x-request-id in lowercase in a few places — consider normalizing casing to match runtime examples. :robot_face:
docs-lint-bot: snippet-check failed on line 12: code-fence not closed. Also flagged an inline example URL that points to staging. Please fix before preview.
sara.t: PII/security note — if we document logs containing custom IDs, we should add a caution about not sending user PII in headers. We need a one-liner: "Do not include PII in headers; headers may be logged depending on your retention settings."
maria.su: Good call, @sara.t — I'll add that. Also can someone paste a minimal expected logs example (what fields will include X-Request-ID) so I can show it in the migration guide?
kevin.l: Minimal example (what we show in docs):
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-18T14:22:33Z","service":"redwood-agent","request_id":"x-rw-request-id-abc123","x_request_id":"user-provided-123","traceparent":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01","msg":"inference.request.received"}
```
Note: field names are snake_case in our logs. x_request_id will contain the user's X-Request-ID if provided.
ajohnson: @kevin.l small thing — in Private we don't redact header values by default; customers can enable header redaction via `redwood.agent.config.redact_headers` in their agent config.
maria.su: Perfect — I'll add the snippet + the PII caution and mention the `redact_headers` option. One last thing: CI preview currently fails because of the code fence issue flagged by docs-lint-bot. @ci-bot can you re-run preview after I push the fix?
ci-bot: Docs preview created: https://preview.redwood.dev/1769994321 — preview build will run lint and linkcheck. (build #4521)
docs-lint-bot: Linkcheck failed: found link to staging.example.com in example. Replace with `https://example.com` or a relative path.
maria.su: Fixed fencing + example URL + added the PII note + short note about `redact_headers`. Pushed a tiny commit.
ci-bot: Preview updated: https://preview.redwood.dev/1769994321 (build #4522) — lint ✅, linkcheck ✅, rendering looks good.
kevin.l: Confirmed — wording is accurate. You can remove the docs hold and request @docs for final review.
maria.su: Removed hold, assigning reviewers: @ajohnson @sara.t. Thanks all — merging once reviewers approve and CI stays green. :rocket:
